name: Central Park
summary: An 843-acre park in the middle of Manhattan with lawns, lakes, walking paths and landmarks such as Bethesda Terrace.
description: Central Park opened in the 1850s and was designed by Frederick Law Olmsted and Calvert Vaux. Visitors can walk or cycle the loop drive, rent a rowboat at the Loeb Boathouse, visit the Conservatory Garden, or relax on the Great Lawn and Sheep Meadow.

name: Statue of Liberty
summary: The copper statue on Liberty Island, reached by ferry from Battery Park. Trips usually include Ellis Island.
description: Dedicated in 1886, the statue was a gift from France. Ferries leave from Battery Park in Manhattan and Liberty State Park in New Jersey. Pedestal and crown access require separate reservations, and visitors pass through security screening before boarding.
opening_hours: Daily; ferry times vary by season

name: Empire State Building
summary: A 1931 Art Deco skyscraper with open-air and indoor observation decks on the 86th and 102nd floors.
description: The Empire State Building was the world's tallest building for about 40 years. Its 86th-floor deck offers 360-degree views of Manhattan. The building's exhibits cover its construction and history.

name: The Metropolitan Museum of Art
summary: One of the world's largest art museums, with collections spanning 5,000 years on Fifth Avenue.
description: The Met's collection includes Egyptian art and the Temple of Dendur, European paintings, arms and armor, and the American Wing. The roof garden is open seasonally. New York State residents and students from New York, New Jersey and Connecticut pay what they wish.
opening_hours: Sunday to Tuesday and Thursday, 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM; Friday and Saturday until 9:00 PM; closed Wednesday

name: Times Square
summary: A busy plaza at Broadway and Seventh Avenue known for its electronic billboards and Broadway theaters nearby.
description: Times Square is the center of the Theater District. The TKTS booth under the red steps sells discounted same-day Broadway tickets. The area is busiest in the evening, when the billboards are most visible.

name: Brooklyn Bridge
summary: An 1883 suspension bridge with a pedestrian promenade between Lower Manhattan and Brooklyn.
description: The elevated promenade is about 1.1 miles long and offers views of the Manhattan skyline and the harbor. Many visitors walk from Manhattan toward DUMBO and Brooklyn Bridge Park.

name: The High Line
address: Gansevoort St to W 34th St, New York, NY
summary: A 1.45-mile elevated park built on a former freight rail line on Manhattan's West Side.
description: The High Line runs from the Meatpacking District to Hudson Yards, with gardens, public art and views of the Hudson River. Entrances are along the route; the southern end is near the Whitney Museum and Chelsea Market.
opening_hours: Daily, 7:00 AM to 10:00 PM; hours vary by season

name: 9/11 Memorial & Museum
summary: Twin reflecting pools on the footprints of the former World Trade Center towers, with a museum below.
description: The outdoor memorial lists the names of the victims of the 2001 and 1993 attacks and is free to visit. The museum documents the events and their aftermath and requires a timed ticket.
opening_hours: Memorial daily, 7:30 AM to 9:00 PM; museum hours vary

name: Museum of Modern Art
summary: MoMA's collection of modern and contemporary art includes works by Van Gogh, Picasso and Warhol.
description: Highlights include The Starry Night, Les Demoiselles d'Avignon and Campbell's Soup Cans. The Abby Aldrich Rockefeller Sculpture Garden is part of the museum.
opening_hours: Daily, 10:30 AM to 5:30 PM; Saturday until 7:00 PM

name: American Museum of Natural History
address: 200 Central Park West, New York, NY 10024
summary: A natural history museum on the Upper West Side known for its dinosaur halls and planetarium.
description: Exhibits include the fossil halls, the blue whale model in the Hall of Ocean Life, the Rose Center for Earth and Space, and the Gilder Center. New York State residents pay what they wish for general admission.
